quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: Parking is not allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcycle rider:

options.text: Feels uncomfortable.
Protects you in a crash.
Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good motorcycle clothing protects you in a crash, keeps you comfortable, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used if you share the lane with another vehicle.
Usually gives good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually gives enough traction for safe riding, except when raining. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: You should inspect your motorcycle:

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Twice a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This takes just a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you enter traffic.

questions.question: Your lane position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Has little impact on whether other drivers see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Takes only a few minutes.
Takes about an hour.
Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: You should inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This will usually take only a few minutes.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Only use the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: You are most likely to have a collision:

options.text: At an intersection.
When riding in a group.
On the expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the highest risk of conflict between you and other traffic.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:

options.text: Is always the left side.
Is always the right side.
Changes based on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on the situation.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Change your position as needed for the situation.

questions.question: To shift to a higher gear, you must:

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push it down.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift it.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Be ready to brake to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, choose a position that makes you visible to other drivers and be ready to brake. Slow down as you approach. Do not speed up or change position suddenly, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: Noise from wind:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.
Can cause permanent hearing damage.
Is never dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear proper ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: Before riding with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Get off the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, avoid the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chance of an accident by:

options.text: Not looking ahead for hazards.
Not using turn signals so other drivers are not distracted.
Being visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid a collision, be visible, signal your intentions clearly, keep space between you and other vehicles, watch ahead, and be ready to react to any hazard.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit with your arms straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms steer rather than hold you up. Your elbows should bend slightly at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same as normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer needs a longer following distance. The extra weight means it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals.
Use proper lane positions.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others, signal your moves, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: Which is not a way to control a motorcycle in a turn?

options.text: Speed up through the turn.
Slow down before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before you enter it. Look through the turn toward where you want to go, press the handlebar to lean the right way, and gently roll the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the other vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
Has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may signal the other driver to move back into your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
How much alcohol you drink
Body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect blood alcohol content (BAC) are how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Firm footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Dark-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible, even during daytime riding. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip. Use only the rear brake to control your speed during the U-turn.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Keep applying the front brake.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during a quick stop, release the front brake immediately and then press it firmly again. Use both brakes if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, you should:

options.text: Not wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors when riding to make yourself easier to see, even in daylight.

questions.question: When you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to where other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph, like farm equipment or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: Wearing what gives you the best chance to avoid serious injury in a crash?

options.text: Face or eye protection.
A baseball cap.
Sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury. A plastic face shield protects your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Never hold onto the rider.
Not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. They can also hold onto secure handholds if available.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of a motorcycle hitting other traffic?

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be careful when approaching intersections.

questions.question: When it is raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially when rain first starts. Oil from cars hasn't washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position. A smart rider changes position as conditions change.

questions.question: If you must shift gears while turning, you should:

options.text: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
Shift in the curve rather than before it.
Use this as the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before starting a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can cause a skid.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you to see farther using its lights.
Keep your normal speed to reduce the risk of being hit from behind.
Slow down and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance. You cannot see as far ahead. You need extra time and space to react to dangers.
